issues.description: Identifier inconsistency: the exercise specification and template expect concrete classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat, but the solution repository provides classes named SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat while leaving Seal.java, Pig.java, and Goat.java empty. Specifically, the problem statement UML and tasks refer to Seal/Pig/Goat as concrete subclasses of Animal, and the template Main.java (commented) instantiates Seal, Pig, and Goat. In the solution repository only SpaceSeal/SpacePig/SpaceGoat are implemented and Seal.java, Pig.java, Goat.java contain no implementations. This mismatch prevents a student or an automated grader from relying on the solution artifacts to find the expected class names and can cause confusion or compilation/runtime mismatches if tests or examples refer to Seal/Pig/Goat.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the class names consistent between specification/template and solution. Option A (preferred for minimal change): add concrete Seal, Pig, and Goat classes in the solution repository that implement the same behavior as the existing SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat (these can delegate to or copy the implementations), so Seal/Pig/Goat exist with the expected constructors and methods. Option B: rename SpaceSeal/SpacePig/SpaceGoat to Seal/ Pig/ Goat throughout the solution repository and update any references. Option C (if intentional): update the problem statement and template to reference SpaceSeal/SpacePig/SpaceGoat consistently. Ensure Main, UML, and test expectations use the exact same class names as implemented in the solution.

issues.description: The exercise asks students to implement animal classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat (problem statement and the template Main reference these exact names), but the solution repository provides implementations named SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat. Concept: concrete animal classes representing Seal/Pig/Goat. Problem statement & template identifier: Seal, Pig, Goat. Solution repository identifiers: SpaceSeal, SpacePig, SpaceGoat. This mismatch prevents a direct mapping between the required class names and the solution's classes, may break or confuse the provided Main example (which constructs Seal/Pig/Goat), and changes runtime outputs that use animal.getClass().getSimpleName() (e.g., the song will print "SpaceSeal" instead of the expected "Seal"). Students comparing their implementations to the solution or trying to run the sample Main will be blocked or confused by the naming difference.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the class names consistent across artifacts. Preferred options: (1) Rename the solution classes to Seal, Pig, Goat (SpaceSeal -> Seal, SpacePig -> Pig, SpaceGoat -> Goat) and update their constructors and usages accordingly; or (2) Add thin wrapper classes named Seal/Pig/Goat in the solution repository that extend/delegate to SpaceSeal/SpacePig/SpaceGoat so the expected names exist; or (3) If the 'Space' prefix is intentional, update the problem statement and template (including Main and any examples) to reference SpaceSeal/SpacePig/SpaceGoat and clarify that getClass().getSimpleName() will include the prefix. Ensure the singFarmSong output expectations are aligned with the chosen naming so students are not confused by differing printed types.
